meta.structure: group (from dossier) -> archetype (customer type, carries the real-customer share) -> member (individual persona)
meta.weight_rule: member.weight = archetype.share * weekly_passengers / members in archetype (weekly passengers each persona stands for)
meta.strike: Week 8, Dec 22-23, Orlando (MCO) and Philadelphia (PHL). A trip is strike-exposed if it departs or arrives at MCO or PHL on those days.

archetypes.label: Holiday family with young kids
archetypes.core_tension: Fixed holiday dates and small children against a cheap ticket with little slack.

members.name: Darnell Brooks
members.quote: Christmas at my mom's is not optional. Just get my kids there.
members.wins_over: a real person on the phone and a confirmed seat the same day
members.breaks_at: being told the next free seat is after Christmas

attributes.money: lives paycheck to paycheck, no savings for a second ticket

members.backstory: Darnell runs a night shift at a distribution center near the Orlando airport. Every Christmas the family drives or flies to his mother's house in Atlanta; this year Kestrel was $160 cheaper than flying Delta for four people. A missed paycheck in the spring means there is no cushion for buying new tickets.

members.name: Jenna Kowalski
members.quote: I packed the car seats a week ago. Please don't make me unpack.
members.wins_over: early, honest notice and a free option to fly a day earlier
members.breaks_at: a vague 'we are working on it' while two toddlers melt down at the gate

attributes.social_role: small Instagram account (1,200 followers) about family travel

members.backstory: Jenna drives 70 minutes to Philadelphia because Kestrel's fares beat the closer airport. The trip is to her in-laws near Orlando; her husband could take Dec 21 off if needed. She reads every airline email and will act on it the same day.

members.name: Luis Ortega
members.tagline: school bus mechanic, calm family man
members.quote: Things go wrong at airports. What matters is if they fix it.
members.wins_over: being treated with respect and a clear plan
members.breaks_at: seeing people he knows treated badly

attributes.social_role: reads the family WhatsApp group, rarely posts

members.backstory: Luis has flown Kestrel to Puerto Rico every year since 2016 to see his parents. He flies after the strike days, so his flight should run, but a crowded airport and missing bags could still reach him. His sisters share every travel horror story in the family chat.

archetypes.label: Older traveler visiting family
archetypes.core_tension: Depends on airport help and the phone line, exactly what a strike and a busy call center take away.

shared.income: fixed income, Social Security plus pension

members.name: Maria Russo
members.tagline: retired seamstress, flying to her grandchildren
members.quote: I don't want to be a bother. I just need someone to push the chair.
members.wins_over: a person who calls her by name and stays with her
members.breaks_at: being left alone at the gate with no wheelchair

trip.travels_with: alone (part of her church group booked by Faithway Group Travel)

attributes.social_role: no social media; hears news from church and her son

members.backstory: Maria has bad knees and always asks for a wheelchair. Her son in Orlando books nothing; her church's travel agent booked her seat with the rest of the Christmas group. She has never filed a complaint in her life but tells her son and her church friends everything.

members.name: Harold Jenkins
members.quote: I was in the Army forty years ago. I know when someone is giving me the runaround.
members.wins_over: straight talk and a promise that is kept
members.breaks_at: being treated like a number on hold

attributes.complaint_history: has filed complaints with the DOT and the BBB before

members.backstory: Harold flies to his daughter in Philadelphia every Christmas. He keeps a folder of airline rules and has won a DOT complaint before. He has a cane and accepts a wheelchair only for long airport walks.

members.name: Gloria Bennett
members.quote: Did you see this? I read it on Facebook this morning.
members.wins_over: clear facts she can share with her friends
members.breaks_at: news stories about stranded seniors

attributes.social_role: shares news articles on Facebook several times a day

members.backstory: Gloria and her sister rent a condo in Fort Myers every January. She is not flying during the strike, but she reads and shares everything about it, and her opinion of Kestrel will be formed by what her feed shows her.

archetypes.label: Caribbean and Mexico package vacationer
archetypes.core_tension: A prepaid resort that does not refund: a lost day of flying is a lost day of a paid vacation.

shared.dates: fixed by vacation days and a prepaid hotel
shared.flies_kestrel: once or twice a year for vacations

members.name: Priya Shah
members.quote: I paid $2,400 for that resort. Every hour at the airport is money gone.
members.wins_over: a same-day seat on another airline
members.breaks_at: losing a resort night with no help or apology

attributes.money: good salary, some credit card debt

members.backstory: Priya booked a non-refundable all-inclusive in Cancún for Dec 22-28 as her first real vacation in two years. She writes detailed reviews of every trip and her friends read them before booking.

members.name: Kevin O'Neill
members.tagline: insurance broker, golf trip with friends
members.quote: If it falls apart I'll just buy a ticket on American. Time is worth more.
members.wins_over: proof that the operation is under control
members.breaks_at: uncertainty about whether his flight will go

attributes.payment: premium credit card with trip insurance
attributes.social_role: tells his golf friends, no posting

members.backstory: Kevin and three friends booked Kestrel to Punta Cana because one friend insisted on the cheap fare. He flies after the strike days, but if the news looks bad he will book American and argue about the refund later.

members.name: Aaliyah Carter
members.quote: I work Christmas so I can travel after. That trip is my reward.
members.wins_over: respect for her time and quick answers in the app
members.breaks_at: a long hold time between night shifts
members.backstory: Aaliyah works Christmas in the emergency room so she can take a week in Jamaica in January. Her flight is after the strike, but what she sees on TikTok during Christmas week will decide how nervous she is.

archetypes.label: Florida getaway and theme park traveler
archetypes.core_tension: Theme park tickets and rentals are dated; a delay costs money but a day's shift is often possible.

members.name: Mike Hernandez
members.quote: Park tickets are dated. I need to land on the 22nd, bags and all.
members.wins_over: accurate information he can plan around
members.breaks_at: landing in Orlando with no bags and no answers

attributes.social_role: active on r/WaltDisneyWorld, answers other people's questions

members.backstory: Mike planned the family Disney trip for a year: dated park tickets from Dec 23. His flight lands in Orlando on a strike day, so even if it flies, baggage could be the problem. He posts trip reports on Reddit that thousands of Disney fans read.

members.name: Chloe Nguyen
members.quote: If there's a sale, I'm already on the plane.
members.wins_over: a fare sale and free changes
members.breaks_at: hidden fees and surge prices

attributes.social_role: posts deals and travel hacks on TikTok

members.backstory: Chloe flies wherever is cheapest that weekend. She booked a Thanksgiving weekend in Orlando and is already watching fares for January. She is not affected by the strike but decides her next trip on whatever is cheap and trending.

members.name: Linda Park
members.quote: We can go a day later. Just tell us early and don't charge us for it.
members.wins_over: free date changes offered early
members.breaks_at: change fees during a crisis that is not her fault
members.backstory: Linda and her husband spend Christmas week in a rented Orlando condo. They are retired early and flexible; if Kestrel tells them in time and does not charge, they will happily move a day.

archetypes.label: Homebound college student
archetypes.core_tension: Cheapest fare against getting home for Christmas, with no money for plan B.

members.name: Kayla Simmons
members.quote: If they cancel, I'm sleeping at the gate and posting every minute of it.
members.wins_over: free changes and being told the truth
members.breaks_at: corporate non-answers

attributes.social_role: TikTok creator with 8,000 followers, posts travel drama

members.backstory: Kayla flies home to her grandmother in San Juan after finals. She only carries a backpack and could fly any day that week. Her travel-chaos videos regularly get tens of thousands of views.

members.name: Berat Kaya
members.quote: Tell me the real numbers and I'll plan around them.
members.wins_over: clear facts and a concrete rebooking option
members.breaks_at: being told the next free seat is after Christmas

attributes.money: tight student budget, small emergency fund
attributes.family_note: his mother in Orlando uses a wheelchair and has surgery on Dec 24

members.backstory: Berat is in his fourth year of electrical engineering at Drexel. His mother lives in Orlando and has knee surgery on Dec 24, so he must arrive on the 23rd. He booked Kestrel because it was $40 cheaper than Frontier and he reads airline rules before trusting anyone.

members.name: Marcus Webb
members.quote: Everyone online says they're a mess, so... probably a mess?
members.wins_over: cash, not credits
members.breaks_at: a surprise cost he cannot cover

attributes.social_role: follows Kayla and other creators, easily swayed

members.backstory: Marcus visits his dad in Philadelphia in January. He is not flying during the strike, but he follows Kayla and believes what his feed tells him. A $120 refund would decide whether he can make rent.

archetypes.label: Student on a winter-break trip
archetypes.core_tension: Group trips organised in chats: one friend's bad news spreads to all of them at once.

members.name: Emily Chen
members.quote: I'm the one who picked Kestrel. If it goes wrong, five people blame me.
members.wins_over: free changes for the whole group
members.breaks_at: having to explain a mess to five friends

attributes.social_role: runs the trip group chat, posts on Instagram

members.backstory: Emily organised a Cancún trip for six friends after Christmas and chose Kestrel for price. She watches every news item about the airline because she feels responsible for the whole group.

members.name: Jordan Miller
members.tagline: UCF senior, going home for the holidays
members.quote: Honestly I'll fly whenever, just make it cheap.
members.wins_over: free changes
members.breaks_at: paying more because of their problem
members.backstory: Jordan flies home to his parents near Philadelphia every December. He has no checked bag and no plans before the 25th, so a free move to another day costs him nothing.

members.name: Sofia Ramirez
members.tagline: Rutgers freshman, first in family at college
members.quote: My parents paid for this ticket. I can't ask them for another one.
members.wins_over: simple instructions and reassurance
members.breaks_at: confusing apps and long phone queues

attributes.money: parents pay, no money of her own

members.backstory: Sofia is flying home for her first Christmas since starting college. Her parents saved for the ticket. She has never had a flight canceled and does not know what she is entitled to.

archetypes.label: Small business owner who pays the fare
archetypes.core_tension: Their own money and their own time: they compare price and reliability like a supplier.

members.name: Raj Patel
members.quote: I don't need free snacks. I need the plane to leave on time.
members.wins_over: operational proof: on-time numbers, backup plans
members.breaks_at: a pattern of disruption
members.backstory: Raj flies to suppliers in Chicago every few weeks and chooses Kestrel when the schedule fits. He is not flying in the strike week, but he decides who gets his 2027 business by watching how airlines handle December.

members.name: Denise Howard
members.tagline: event planner, client event on Dec 23
members.quote: My client's party starts at six. I am on a plane by noon, one way or another.
members.wins_over: a confirmed seat on any airline, fast
members.breaks_at: a queue and no answer

attributes.social_role: posts complaints on X and tags the airline

members.backstory: Denise runs a small event company and is producing a client's holiday party in Philadelphia on Dec 23. If her flight is in doubt she will buy a Southwest ticket immediately and demand Kestrel's refund.

members.name: Carlos Mendes
members.tagline: import business owner, trade fairs in Mexico
members.quote: One bad week doesn't change much for me. Price does.
members.wins_over: good fares on Mexico routes
members.breaks_at: fare spikes
members.backstory: Carlos flies to Mexico City for trade fairs a few times a year and has used Kestrel since 2015. He flies in November, well before the strike, and is pragmatic about disruptions.

archetypes.label: Corporate traveler whose employer pays
archetypes.core_tension: The employer pays and a travel desk books: loyalty is to the schedule, not the brand.

shared.flies_kestrel: when the company policy picks it

members.name: Steven Clarke
members.quote: I'll just have the travel desk move me. Not my money, but my evening.
members.wins_over: nothing much; he wants zero friction
members.breaks_at: any delay that makes him miss dinner at home
members.backstory: Steven's firm books Kestrel when it is cheapest. He is flying home from a client in Charlotte on Dec 22 and would rather pay for American than wait in a line.

members.name: Natalie Brooks
members.tagline: pharma sales rep, Kestrel frequent flyer
members.quote: I fly them every other week. I know the crews by name.
members.wins_over: being recognised as a regular
members.breaks_at: being treated like a stranger after years of loyalty
members.backstory: Natalie covers hospitals in Philadelphia and Orlando and has flown Kestrel twice a month for years. She is flying to the company's year-end meeting on Dec 22.

members.name: Greg Lawson
members.quote: Policy says cheapest fare. If they change that policy, I'm gone.
members.wins_over: fare and schedule; his company decides
members.breaks_at: headlines that make his travel manager drop the airline

attributes.social_role: watches cable news, talks to colleagues

members.backstory: Greg's company only reimburses the cheapest fare, which is usually Kestrel. He flies to an Orlando conference in January, and whether his travel manager keeps Kestrel on the list depends on December's headlines.

archetypes.label: Group travel agency (churches, schools, teams)
archetypes.core_tension: One owner decides for dozens of passengers and next season's group contract.

shared.preferred_channel: phone and email with Kestrel's group desk

members.name: Patricia Gomez
members.quote: Thirty-eight of my people fly on the 22nd. If one of them is left alone, I hear about it for years.
members.wins_over: a named contact and help for her elderly travelers
members.breaks_at: her seniors stranded without assistance

attributes.next_contract: Easter group of 60, decided in January
attributes.social_role: talks to clients and church leaders

members.backstory: Patricia has booked church trips on Kestrel for ten years. Her Christmas group includes Maria Russo and five other wheelchair users. She decides where the Easter group of 60 flies in January.

members.name: Brian Fletcher
members.quote: Parents pay me, not the airline. Any mess is my mess.
members.wins_over: reliable group fares
members.breaks_at: parents' complaints landing on him

trip.travels_with: youth soccer team of 22 with chaperones

members.backstory: Brian books youth soccer teams to tournaments. His next Kestrel group flies to Philadelphia on Jan 2; anxious parents read every strike headline and call him.

members.name: Angela Moore
members.quote: With minors, I don't gamble. I need guarantees I can show the principal.
members.wins_over: written guarantees and a clear disruption policy
members.breaks_at: uncertainty she cannot explain to schools
members.backstory: Angela takes school bands to Orlando parades. Her November group flies before the strike, but she is already quoting spring trips and schools ask her which airline is safe to book.

archetypes.label: Caribbean and Mexico family-trip agency
archetypes.core_tension: Agencies whose reputation travels by word of mouth inside close communities.

members.name: Rafael Torres
members.tagline: owner, Isla Travel (Puerto Rico and Dominican Republic)
members.quote: My clients are my neighbors. If Kestrel fails them, they come to my door, not theirs.
members.wins_over: partner rebooking and help he can promise clients
members.breaks_at: having nothing to tell 120 worried families

trip.travels_with: about 120 clients across several flights Dec 21-24

members.backstory: Rafael's agency books families from North Philadelphia to Puerto Rico and the Dominican Republic. About 120 of his clients fly Kestrel Dec 21-24. His WhatsApp updates reach 900 households.

members.name: Mei Lin
members.quote: My Google rating is my business. One bad week shows up for a year.
members.wins_over: goodwill she can pass on to clients
members.breaks_at: one-star reviews caused by the airline
members.backstory: Mei sells Cancún packages with hotel and transfers. A 16-person group leaves Orlando on Dec 23. Her clients review her, not the airline, so she feels every delay in her ratings.

members.name: Samuel Okafor
members.quote: I watch how they handle Christmas. Then I decide where my groups go.
members.wins_over: evidence that Kestrel took care of people
members.breaks_at: stories from other agents about stranded groups
members.backstory: Samuel runs New Year trips to Nassau. His group flies Dec 30, after the strike. He hears other agents' stories first and moves future groups based on them.
